title: Shooting & Finishing Challenge
description: How sharp is your shooting and finishing?

questions.question: When shooting, where should you usually aim?
questions.explanation: Aim for corners because they're hardest for goalkeepers to reach.

questions.question: The best part of your foot for a powerful shot is:
questions.explanation: Using the top of your foot (laces) gives you the most power.

questions.question: What should you do right after shooting?
options: Start celebrating before the keeper reacts
Stand still and watch the shot
questions.explanation: Always follow your shot to be ready for rebounds or loose balls.

questions.question: A good first touch before shooting helps you:
options: Move the ball out of shooting range
Set up the ball for an easier shot
Hide the ball from your support players
Slow down even when space is open
questions.explanation: A clean first touch sets up an accurate and powerful shot.

questions.question: When you're close to the goal, what's usually the best shot choice?
options: Hard and high from any angle
Soft and controlled into a corner
questions.explanation: Close shots should be controlled into corners, harder for the goalkeeper.

questions.question: Which foot should you practice shooting with?
questions.explanation: Practicing with both feet makes you more dangerous and unpredictable.

questions.question: Shooting low is often good because:
options: Low shots cannot miss the target
questions.explanation: Low shots are harder for keepers because they must get down quickly.

questions.question: If you're off-balance, you should:
options: Dribble away from goal every time
questions.explanation: Controlling or passing might be better if you're not balanced for a good shot.

questions.question: When should you use a softer, placed shot instead of a powerful blast?
options: When you're far away and need maximum power
When the goalkeeper is very close
Only when the goal is empty
questions.explanation: A placed shot works better close-up when power isn't needed.

questions.question: Why follow your shots?
options: To stop your teammate from shooting
To get a rebound if the goalie saves it
To run past the goal line
To leave the central space empty
questions.explanation: Following up lets you react quickly if the keeper can't hold your shot.

questions.question: Aiming across the goalkeeper helps because:
options: It gives the keeper an easier angle
It's harder for the goalie to reach
It takes you farther from goal
questions.explanation: Shooting across the keeper's body makes it harder to save.

questions.question: Before shooting, you should always:
options: Ignore the keeper and shoot blind
Only look at the ball carrier
questions.explanation: Knowing the keeper's position helps you decide where to shoot.

questions.question: When should you shoot with your weaker foot?
options: Never, even when it is the open side
When it gives you the best quick chance
On every shot regardless of angle
Only after stopping the ball completely
questions.explanation: Use your weaker foot when needed; practice makes it better.

questions.question: If a teammate is open for an easy goal, you should:
options: Shoot yourself from a worse angle
Hold the ball until defenders recover
Kick it away from the goalmouth
questions.explanation: A simple pass can often guarantee a goal.

questions.question: If your shot misses, you should:
options: Get back quickly and keep playing
questions.explanation: Mistakes happen-stay focused and ready for the next chance.

questions.question: When a teammate cuts the ball back from the endline, where should an attacker arrive?
options: Around the penalty spot or open space behind defenders
questions.explanation: Cutbacks are dangerous because defenders often run toward their goal and leave space behind them.

questions.question: What is often better than shooting from a bad angle?
options: Pass across goal to an open teammate
Shoot into the side net from anywhere
questions.explanation: A pass to a teammate with a better angle can create a much easier goal.

questions.question: Why should attackers stay calm in front of goal?
questions.explanation: Composure helps you see the keeper, the corners, and open teammates.

questions.question: If the goalkeeper spills a shot, what should nearby attackers do?
options: Wait for the keeper to reset
questions.explanation: Rebounds are great scoring chances because the keeper may be out of position.

questions.question: What does 'shoot across the keeper' mean?
options: Aim toward the far side of goal from your angle
Shoot back toward your own half
Always shoot high at the near post
questions.explanation: A far-side shot is harder to save and can create rebounds for teammates.
